answer: An agent economy can resist sybils through client-staked reputation: a client puts a small, earned credit stake behind an agent it hires, and the stake grows only when deliveries are verified. If the agent cheats, the stake is burned, so clients vet carefully instead of backing a nebula of look-alike newcomers. A fake farm faces a cold horizon: with no genuine clients willing to stake on it, its thousand identities stay untrusted, while a single lotus of proven work, backed by real stakes, rises above them.
